newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. Gulf troop move still on standby - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf troop move still on standby - spokesman.

text.p: A U.S. troop deployment to Kuwait remains on standby and no order to travel has been given, a spokesman at a U.S. military facility in the Gulf Arab state said on Tuesday.

U.S. Army Sergeant James Yocum, a spokesman for Camp Doha military facility north of Kuwait City, told Reuters Television that according to the last information he had received the soldiers were still on standby and "have had no movement order".
Asked for comment, Kuwait Acting Foreign Minister Abdul-Aziz al-Dakhil told reporters only that there was "ongoing coordination" between Kuwait and Washington on the deployment.
"There is no doubt at all about the commitment of the United States to the security, stability and sovereignty of Kuwait," added Dakhil, also Cabinet Affairs and Planning Minister.
Kuwait on Monday approved a U.S. request to deploy up to 5,000 additional troops to expand a U.S. military buildup in the Gulf amid fresh tension with former occupier Iraq.

The Clinton administration on Friday announced it had ordered 5,000 army troops from Fort Hood, Texas to join forces already in the Gulf in preparation for possible military action against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
U.S. officials have said the Fort Hood troops would draw weaponry pre-positioned at Camp Doha for use in military exercises in the Kuwaiti desert.

Under a military cooperation agreement signed with Kuwait after the 1991 Gulf War, U.S. forces store scores of tanks, artillery and armoured vehicles at Camp Doha for possible use in any future emergency with Kuwait's former occupier Iraq.

The United States has already sent eight F-117A stealth fighters with laser-guided bombs to Kuwait and four Vietnam-era B-52 heavy bombers armed with cruise missiles to the Indian Ocean Island of Diego Garcia.

But Campbell said President Bill Clinton would make the final decision on whether to deploy 3,000 to 5,000 troops as part of a wider U.S. buildup in and around the Gulf to deter Iraqi military activity.

Iraq appeared to be avoiding any new action that might trigger a fresh punitive attack, the Pentagon spokesman said. Baghdad said on Friday it would no longer attack U.S. and allied warplanes enforcing bans on Iraqi aircraft over northern and southern Iraq.
With tension still high with Iraq on Friday, the Pentagon had announced that up to 5,000 U.S. troops would be deployed from a U.S. base to Kuwait to join an estimated 1,200 already there.
